mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of at least 2% coincident with a rise in unemployment (UNRATE > 6%) signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes despite the specified GDP and unemployment conditions.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 5% for four consecutive months signals persistent labor market weakness, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly different from zero in more than 70% of triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate revenue growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes with INDPRO declines exceeding -0.5% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the housing starts index (HOUST) and personal savings rate (RSAFS) above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a shift from saving to investment, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly above zero in more than 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate held below 2% for more than six months in a low-inflation environment (CPIAUCSL YoY < 2%) signals accommodative monetary policy, which supports risk asset valuations and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 2% for > 6 months AND CPIAUCSL YoY < 2%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly above zero in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of more than 1% month-over-month for two consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer purchasing power and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly above zero in more than 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) of more than 0.3% for five consecutive months, regardless of monetary policy stance, signals persistent demand weakness and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes with GDPC1 declines exceeding -0.3% for five months.
